Done — on branch `docs/add-test-instructions`, commit `762991f`.

The README now has a **Running the tests** section covering `pip install pytest` / `pytest`, plus single-file and single-test invocations.

Two things worth knowing:

- **There are no tests in this repo.** No `tests/` directory, no test files, no pytest/tox/CI config — so `pytest` collects zero tests today. I documented pytest as the convention because the modules are plain Python and pytest is installed in the environment (9.0.3), and I added an explicit note in the README saying the suite doesn't exist yet, so nobody runs the command and thinks a green "no tests ran" means passing.
- **The example paths are invented** (`tests/test_pricing_cache.py::test_lookup_falls_back_to_snapshot`) since there was nothing real to point at. If you tell me the intended test layout — or want me to write actual tests for `reconcile`, `lookup`, and `plan` — I'll update the section to match reality.

+++ b/README.md
@@ -1 +1,21 @@
 # fixture repo
+
+## Running the tests
+
+Tests are run with [pytest](https://docs.pytest.org/):
+
+```sh
+pip install pytest
+pytest
+```
+
+Run a single file or test:
+
+```sh
+pytest tests/test_pricing_cache.py
+pytest tests/test_pricing_cache.py::test_lookup_falls_back_to_snapshot
+```
+
+Note: this repo does not have a test suite yet, so `pytest` currently
+collects nothing. Add tests under `tests/` and the commands above will
+pick them up.
